claims.text: Tailored thermo-mechanical processing can promote formation of an in situ duplex lamellar microstructure in a refractory high-entropy alloy.
A duplex lamellar microstructure will enhance both strength and plasticity relative to a monolithic single-phase alloy.
Primarily single-phase refractory high-entropy alloys typically exhibit an inverse relationship between strength and ductility.
Casting, rolling, and annealing cycles can be tailored to induce a dual-phase lamellar microstructure.
Controlled heating and deformation can preserve phase stability and avoid deleterious brittle phases in refractory high-entropy alloys.
The duplex lamellar microstructure acts as an in situ composite.
Phase boundaries in the duplex structure impede dislocation motion and thereby increase strength.
The duplex architecture produces a hierarchical constraint effect during deformation.
Interfaces in the duplex architecture arrest microcracks or inhibit crack propagation.
The duplex architecture enhances plasticity through effective energy dissipation across phase interfaces.
The processed refractory alloy will have higher yield strength than the conventionally processed baseline.
The processed refractory alloy will have greater ductility than the conventionally processed baseline.
BCC-dominated refractory alloys generally combine high strength with limited ductility, whereas FCC-dominated refractory alloys have greater plasticity but lower strength.
The proposed intervention should apply broadly to refractory high-entropy alloys containing multiple principal refractory elements under similar thermo-mechanical conditions.
The effectiveness of the intervention depends on alloy composition, phase stability, phase volume fractions, interface characteristics, and the scale and uniformity of the duplex structure.
